hook_text: Why is Mbombela warmer than George? Grab a torch and find out.
clip_script: Shine a torch straight down: a small, bright spot. Tilt it: a big, dim patch. Same light, spread thin. That is the sun. Near the equator it shines almost straight down; further south it shines at a slant. Mbombela sits near the Tropic of Capricorn, at about twenty-five and a half degrees south. George sits at about thirty-four. In January, Mbombela averages about twenty-four degrees, George about twenty. Here is the twist: Mbombela is higher above sea level, which should make it cooler, and it is still warmer. That is how strong latitude is. And it decides the rain too: summer storms in Mbombela, rain in every month in George.
visual_style: A whiteboard torch beam drawn straight and then tilted, then a map of South Africa with two thermometers rising to different heights.
pacing: A quick demo, then two snappy comparisons and a twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and test latitude with your own torch.
